Wrote the verified solution to `/home/kara/solution.md`.

## Diagnosis

`-overlay` is a **build/compile-time** mapping for the `go` toolchain. It does not redirect the process filesystem at runtime. A test that locates its package dir and scans it with `os.ReadFile`/`os.ReadDir` reads the **original** bytes, so an overlay mutant of `read.go` is invisible → false `PASS`, invalid control.

## Fix (verified end-to-end)

1. **Env-var override in the scanner** — `scanRoots()` returns `filepath.SplitList(os.Getenv("DAGGER_PROJECTION_SCAN_ROOTS"))` when set, else the package dir via `runtime.Caller(0)`. Forbidden literal assembled at runtime (`"json" + "." + "Unmarshal"`) so the test doesn't trip itself.
2. **Stage the mutant as real files** in a fresh scratch dir and run:
   ```
   DAGGER_PROJECTION_SCAN_ROOTS=/tmp/mutant_scan_root \
     go test -count=1 -run TestNoReadJSONAutoInTheProjectionPath ./src/projection/
   ```
3. **Keep `-overlay` for build-layer mutants** (constants/branches the compiled test observes), and keep a **no-override control that must PASS**.

## Verification results

| Run | Result |
|---|---|
| no-override control | `ok` |
| overlay mutant | `ok` (mutant invisible — the bug) |
| real-file mutant via override | `FAIL ... forbidden auto JSON read in /tmp/mutant_scan_root/read.go:12` naming `projection_test.go:45` |
| control after fix | `ok` |
| overlay build-layer mutant (`version.go` 1→2) | `FAIL ... schema version = 2, want 1` |
| baseline build-layer | `ok` |

The markdown includes the full test/scanner code, staging script, a pitfalls section (colons via `filepath.SplitList`, fresh scratch dir per mutant, staging the whole package, combine overlay+override only when compiled behavior must also change), and the exact commands.

signatures.description: A mutant staged with go test -overlay does not trip a test that reads its own source from disk. The overlay replaces the COMPILER input; the assertion walked the package directory with os.ReadFile at runtime, so the mutant bytes never reached the check and the control falsely read PASS. Two distinct layers: build inputs (overlay-able) vs runtime filesystem reads (not overlay-able).
